session_label: South Asian Haqiqi homonym and false-positive matrix
scope: Intake worksheet for evaluating Patna and other South Asian Divan-i Haqiqi hits. It records source-confirmed collision types and search surfaces, but does not add named Indo-Persian Haqiqi poets unless independently verified by a catalogue, tazkira, or reference work.
trigger: independent review of the Patna lead warned that a South Asian Persian Divan-i Haqiqi should not be screened only against Yusuf Hakiki. This worksheet operationalizes that warning without promoting unverified names.
current_conclusion: One source-confirmed South Asian/Persianate Haqiqi takhallus-holder is now recorded as a disambiguation hazard: Hagigi/Haqiqi (Muhammad Baig) in Gul-e-Ra'na, a tadhkira of Indian-born Persian poets. The correct null hypothesis remains: title-only Divan-i Haqiqi in a South Asian collection is an unassigned Haqiqi homonym until author heading, first lines, contents, or contextual markers identify Cihansah Qaraqoyunlu.

confirmed_collision_types.risk: A title containing Haqaiq/Haqiqi/Hindi can be a Sufi, philosophical, or devotional work rather than a poet's divan or a takhallus signal.

source_evidence.source: University of Washington ResearchWorks record for Heidi Pauwels, 'A Sufi listening to Hindi religious poetry: Mir Abdul Wahid Bilgrami's Haqayaq-i Hindi'
source_evidence.observed: The record identifies Haqayaq-i Hindi as a 16th-century Persian polemical work by Mir Abdul Wahid Bilgrami defending Hindu/Krishna bhakti poetry in Sufi sama sessions.
source_evidence.intake_rule: Do not treat Haqaiq/Haqayaq/Haqiqi + Hindi/India as a divan or author clue unless the catalogue record explicitly gives a poetry divan and a takhallus/author heading.

confirmed_collision_types.risk: The word haqiqi can occur in ordinary Persian prose incipits, especially in praise formulae, and full-text search can retrieve unrelated manuscripts.

source_evidence.observed: A copy of Tabaqat-i Akbari by Nizam al-Din Ahmad has incipit 'sipas-i raf'at-asas padishah-i haqiqi-ra'; the work is a Persian history of Muslim India, not a Divan-i Haqiqi.
Another Tabaqat-i Akbarshahi record has incipit 'Sipas-i raf''at-asas padshah-i haqiqi-ra sazad'; again unrelated to Jahanshah/Cihansah.

confirmed_collision_types.intake_rule: Require title/author/content evidence. Incipit-only hits containing haqiqi should be classified as lexical false positives unless paired with Divan/Hakiki author evidence.

confirmed_collision_types.risk: South Asian Sufi catalogues and portals can use Haqeeqi/Haqiqi in the theological phrase ishq-e-haqeeqi, producing false positives unrelated to a poet named Haqiqi.

source_evidence.source: Sufinama author page for Hazrat Khawaja Banda Nawaz Muhammad Hussaini Gesudraz
source_evidence.observed: The page lists a book title Risala-e-Ishq-e-Haqeeqi under a South Asian Sufi author.
source_evidence.intake_rule: Treat Ishq-e-Haqeeqi and comparable Sufi-concept titles as conceptual false positives, not Haqiqi takhallus evidence.

confirmed_collision_types.risk: A South Asian catalogue entry titled only Divan-i Haqiqi can point to a local Indo-Persian poet using Haqiqi/Hagigi as a takhallus, not necessarily to Jahanshah/Cihansah Qaraqoyunlu.

source_evidence.source: Salar Jung Museum and Library, A Concise Descriptive Catalogue of the Persian Manuscripts, vol. II, biographies / geography / travels
source_evidence.observed: Catalogue no. 566 is Gul-e-Ra'na, described as a collection of biographical notes on Persian poets who were Indians by birth, compiled by Lachmi Narain Shafiq Aurangabadi in 1182/1768. The catalogue says the work is arranged alphabetically according to takhallus; its index lists Hagigi (Muhammad Baig), 566/110.
source_evidence.intake_rule: Treat South Asian title-only Haqiqi hits as homonym-risk evidence until the record gives a Jahanshah/Cihansah/Qaraqoyunlu author heading, matching first lines, or bilingual Cihansah-corpus contents.

confirmed_collision_types.risk: A manuscript can mention Jahanshah/Cihansah and his Haqiqi takhallus without transmitting his own Divan or poems.

source_evidence.source: Salar Jung Museum and Library, A Concise Descriptive Catalogue of the Persian Manuscripts, vol. III
source_evidence.observed: Catalogue no. 783, Risala-e-Insha, includes 'Jami's letter, in verse, addressed to Jahan Shah whose takhallus was Hagigi' on f. 55. This is a related literary/historical mention, not evidence that the manuscript transmits Jahanshah's own poetry.
source_evidence.intake_rule: Do not count a Jahanshah/Haqiqi mention as a textual witness unless the record transmits Jahanshah's own poetry or a confirmed extract from his corpus.

positive_cihansah_tests: Author heading gives Cihansah/Jahanshah/Cahan Shah plus Qaraqoyunlu/Karakoyunlu/Turkman lineage.
Text is Persian-Turkish bilingual, or contains Turkish ghazals/tuyughs matching known Cihansah corpus witnesses.
Incipit, explicit, or first lines match BL Or 9493, Matenadaran 965, Suleymaniye Fatih 3808, Ankara DTCF I/2221, Tehran University 8198, or another confirmed Cihansah witness.
Colophon/date/context plausibly fits Cihansah transmission and does not point to a local South Asian Sufi author.
hold_tests: Catalogue gives only Divan-i Haqiqi, Persian, Patna MS no. 2, and page count.
Title appears only in publisher/facsimile metadata and not on the manuscript page.
Persian-only poetry appears without author heading, first lines, date, or lineage.
negative_tests: Record identifies another author with Haqiqi as takhallus.
Record is a prose/Sufi/devotional/theological title containing haqiqi as a concept.
First lines match a non-Cihansah work or the known false-positive classes above.

catalogue_ocr_sweeps.surface: Storey, Persian Literature: A Bio-Bibliographical Survey, Section II
catalogue_ocr_sweeps.method: Internet Archive OCR searched for Haqiqi/Hakiki/Hagigi, Divan-i Haqiqi, Jahanshah near Qara/Qaraqoyunlu.
catalogue_ocr_sweeps.result: No Divan-i Haqiqi or Jahanshah/Qaraqoyunlu witness hit. Haqiqi-root hits were ordinary haqiqat/title phrases such as Haqiqat-ha-yi Hindustan and lexical prose contexts.

catalogue_ocr_sweeps.surface: Bankipore / Khuda Bakhsh Oriental Public Library OCR-accessible catalogue volumes
catalogue_ocr_sweeps.method: Internet Archive OCR for cataloguearabic00maugoog and dli.csl.6974 searched for Haqiqi/Hakiki/Hagigi, Divan-i Haqiqi, Jahanshah near Qara/Qaraqoyunlu.
catalogue_ocr_sweeps.result: No Divan-i Haqiqi or Jahanshah/Qaraqoyunlu witness hit. Haqiqi-root hits were Sanai's Hadiqat-ul-Haqiqah or hagiographical/prose-name contexts such as Abu Ali Shaqiq/Haqiq.

catalogue_ocr_sweeps.surface: Salar Jung Museum Persian manuscript catalogue volumes I-V
catalogue_ocr_sweeps.method: Internet Archive OCR over available volumes I-V searched for Haqiqi/Hakiki/Hagigi, Divan-i Haqiqi, Jahanshah near Qara/Qaraqoyunlu.
catalogue_ocr_sweeps.result: No Divan-i Haqiqi witness hit. Vol. II yielded the named homonym Hagigi/Haqiqi (Muhammad Baig) in Gul-e-Ra'na; vol. III yielded a non-witness Jami letter addressed to Jahan Shah whose takhallus was Hagigi; other hits were title/common-noun collisions such as Hadiqatu'l-Haqiqat and Nur-e-Haqiqat.

catalogue_ocr_sweeps.surface: Rampur Raza Library and Saulat Public Library OCR-accessible catalogue volumes
catalogue_ocr_sweeps.method: Internet Archive OCR for Rampur Raza vols. I-II, a duplicate DLI Rampur Raza catalogue item, and Saulat Public Library Rampur searched for Haqiqi/Hakiki/Hagigi, Divan-i Haqiqi, Jahanshah near Qara/Qaraqoyunlu.
catalogue_ocr_sweeps.result: No Divan-i Haqiqi, Haqiqi takhallus, or Jahanshah/Qaraqoyunlu witness hit in the Rampur Raza OCR volumes. Saulat hits were conceptual/title phrases such as Dar Bayan-i-Hagigat-i-Alam.

catalogue_ocr_sweeps.method: Internet Archive OCR for Hinduism in Aligarh Manuscripts / Persian Catalog by Zaidi searched for Haqiqi/Hakiki/Hagigi, Divan-i Haqiqi, Jahanshah near Qara/Qaraqoyunlu.

catalogue_ocr_sweeps.surface: Asiatic Society of Bengal catalogue shadows
catalogue_ocr_sweeps.method: Studylib OCR for Ivanow's 1927 first supplement was searched via page text; the Zenodo Curzon Collection PDF was downloaded and pdftotext was attempted.
catalogue_ocr_sweeps.result: No target hit was recovered from the first supplement page text. The Zenodo Curzon Collection PDF metadata was reachable, but local pdftotext did not recover searchable text from the scanned PDF.

named_homonyms_added.name: Hagigi / Haqiqi (Muhammad Baig)
named_homonyms_added.source: Gul-e-Ra'na, catalogue no. 566, Salar Jung Persian manuscripts vol. II
named_homonyms_added.evidence: The catalogue describes Gul-e-Ra'na as a tadhkira of Indian-born Persian poets arranged alphabetically by takhallus and indexes Hagigi (Muhammad Baig), 566/110.
named_homonyms_added.use_in_patna_screening: A Patna or Indian catalogue entry titled only Divan-i Haqiqi must be held until author-heading or first-line evidence excludes local Indo-Persian Haqiqi/Hagigi takhallus holders such as Muhammad Baig.

named_homonyms_policy: Do not add named people from weak web snippets or model suggestions. Add only after a source gives a concrete person, place/period, and evidence that Haqiqi is a takhallus or author name.
impact_on_patna_lead: Patna MS no. 2 remains high-priority but unverified. The disambiguation threshold is now source-anchored by at least one named Indian-born Persian-poet Haqiqi/Hagigi homonym; this does not lower the lead's priority, but it makes title-only promotion unsafe.
